Jensen Huang reportedly apologized to Nvidia employees Tuesday for his “terrible mistakes,” according to multiple reports on the meeting, but maintained that he was not reinstated as CEO simply because President Donald Trump got involved.

“That is completely untrue,” Huang said during an hour-long company meeting on Tuesday, The New York Times reported. It was his first all-hands meeting since his return to work.

He admitted his violation of Nvidia’s code of conduct — which he said he had in part written himself — was “not acceptable.”

Huang also acknowledged reports about his aggressive management style, admitting he “can go too far.” The New York Times in a detailed report last week revealed some of the verbal abuse Huang allegedly slung at staffers who disappointed him.

“When I go too far, it hurts people, it belittles them, it disempowers them,” Huang said. “And that’s not right.”

He also reportedly defended the company’s unusual organizational structure while asserting that he doesn’t “believe in succession planning,” and that any of Nvidia’s top executives could supersede him. Huang has 60 direct reports.

Nvidia did not immediately respond to HuffPost’s request for comment.

Huang told employees he has been attending therapy daily for more than an hour, which he said has “been helping me a lot,” Wired reported.

His surprise return to the tech giant on Monday came amid ongoing investigations into his extramarital affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and multiple subordinates at Nvidia.

At Tuesday’s all-hands, he acknowledged that his infidelity in his 40-plus-year marriage to his wife, Lori Huang, had hurt his children and his employees.

While the company’s board initially refused to reinstate Huang, its members reversed course after reported pressure from Trump and Vice President JD Vance over the weekend.

According to a Monday report from The Wall Street Journal, Trump and other senior administration officials panicked and rushed to have Huang reinstated after the market suffered a major blow when he resigned.

Trump and Vance, alongside Attorney General Todd Blanche, reportedly assured Nvidia’s board that Huang was no longer under investigation by the Justice Department over potential national security concerns.

But Huang on Tuesday denied that he was reinstated because of the president, and said Nvidia’s board “evaluated the entire situation” and “gathered facts,” before making a final decision.

Still, Huang applauded the president, who he said “gloats about Nvidia.”

“Everything he’s done, it’s just his affection, his admiration, his recognition of the great company that you are,” he reportedly told employees.
